title: Bugs Roberts writing arrangements with no score
summary: At the studio, Bugs writes whole arrangements part by part without a score while the band rehearses.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh-uh, no. Now, you were speaking of Bugs, Bugs sat in the studio and wrote that arrangements.
Oh, yes. He sat in the studio and

wrote the arrangement. We called him up and he said, I'll have it ready for you, when we got to Chicago, Bugs didn't have nothing ready. And Bugs came -- that's the kind of guy he was. He came down to the studio and wrote the whole, entire arrangement while we was there rehearsing. That's what kind of arranger he was.

And he didn't use the score, you know he'd start off -- he might start off with first trumpet, just by itself. Then he'd -- he might take trombone next. Then he'd start the saxophone, that's how he did it.
Yeah, no score at all. Isn't that right Charles? No score at all.

You see him sitting there, using his fingers, no -- you know he'd write down, I guess he was counting to see -- you know space or what not, you know, and transposing the different -- different keys and what-not, the different instruments, you know, that's how he did.
Some of his arrangements would sound kind of modern today. He used quite a bit of doubling to the arrangements. Bottom, had a lot of bottom (Unintelligible).
